title: Subject reduction (type/FV preservation under β) is used but not stated

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
Proposition prop:step opens with "If M→N then M,N:σ for a common σ" and Theorem thm:main reuses "M→N gives M,N:σ with FV(N)⊆FV(M)". These are subject reduction (type preservation) plus the fact that β-contraction does not introduce free variables. Both are standard for STLC but are neither stated nor cited.

Status: GENUINE but MINOR. For an argument advertised as fully "elementary" and self-contained, this should be recorded as a cited lemma. Crucially it does NOT depend on SN (it is proved by induction on the typing/reduction derivation using the standard substitution-typing lemma: if Γ,x:τ⊢M:σ and Γ⊢N:τ then Γ⊢M[x:=N]:σ), so including it introduces no circularity with the SN goal.

Action: add a one-line citation/statement of (i) subject reduction and (ii) FV(N)⊆FV(M) under M→_β N. No impact on the construction or the main inductions.
